subject: art-design
title: Modernist to Contemporary Photography
welcome_lead: From Steiglitz's straight photography to Sherman's staged self.
meta_desc: A-Level Art & Design: Steiglitz, Cindy Sherman, Jeff Wall, and photo theory.
final_note: A photograph is a fiction with the texture of reality.

walkthroughs.body_html: Alfred Stieglitz championed photography as a fine art at his New York gallery 291 (1905-1917). His own work moved from pictorial soft-focus to crisp 'straight photography' modernism.

Cindy Sherman's Untitled Film Stills (1977-1980) comprise 70 black-and-white photographs in which she stages herself as fictional film heroines, dissolving the boundary between self-portrait and performance.

Jeff Wall's large back-lit colour transparencies — A Sudden Gust of Wind (after Hokusai), The Destroyed Room — borrow scale and lighting from cinema and history painting to construct elaborate tableaux.
